title: The promise gets a working day
notes: Verb card is VERB-1948-PLANT (storyboard: '1948 · PLANT'); the plan's '5 JULY 1948 · PLANT' card does not exist. DATE-5-JULY-1948 is not used: the narration speaks the date and the leaflet itself says 'On 5th July the new National Health Service starts'. If Kai wants the date on screen, swap 09-04 for DATE-5-JULY-1948 at the same clock and move the verb card nowhere (the scene has no other slot).

The leaflet on disk is the SCOTTISH printing ('Issued by the Department of Health for Scotland'). It does NOT contain the plan's line 'It will provide you with all medical, dental and nursing care' (that is the English leaflet). So the push goes to the line this printing has: 'Anyone can use it … no fees to pay' under P6.04, and the storyboard's own picture note, 'He will be paid, out of public funds to which all contribute as taxpayers', under P6.06 ('The staff and suppliers still had to be paid').

Order differs from the plan at P6.05/P6.06: the trolley labelled CHARLEY / PATH LAB (the plan's pick for the whole 'Not free to provide' line) takes P6.05 only; the leaflet's 'He will be paid…' takes P6.06, as the storyboard's picture note asks.

P6.07 is Pop Goes the Weasel's single tracking shot from prams to a post-office counter signed ALLOWANCES, DRAFTS & PENSIONS, then the mother with a baby at the grille: family allowance paid over the counter, not a clinic (the plan called it a clinic window).

The tree fall (P6.09) runs as three pieces across nine seconds: the climb up the ladder, the fall and the ring of stars, then the same man in a hospital bed with his leg in traction. The man who falls is Charley's bald neighbour, not Charley. The source cuts on from the traction bed to calendar pages and a blizzard of banknotes (≈465 s on); stop before them (house rule 3).
Your Very Good Health and New Town are colour cartoons: FILM-43, no grade. Diary for Timothy and Pop Goes the Weasel get GRADE-BW.
No end-credit string for A Diary for Timothy yet (same as scene 11).
